# How a Short Seller Succeeds: The Blueprint for Strategy and Survival

First listed: 2025-07-28 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: How a Short Seller Succeeds: The Blueprint for Strategy and Survival](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t2RyD1M4gmU) - 2025-07-28
- [Substack: The Secrets of the Short Seller Part 2: The Blueprint for Strategy & Survival](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-secrets-of-the-short-seller-part-1f3) - 2025-07-28

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman and Brad Safalow examine short-selling risk through Freshpet, Trupanion and Kinsale. Eisman discloses a Trupanion short, endorses its apparent deterioration and insists on catalysts and surviving countertrend rallies. Most detailed allegations and forecasts belong to Safalow. Later results support slower Freshpet growth and Kinsale premium pressure but contradict the predicted Kinsale underwriting deterioration and weaken Trupanion’s collapse narrative. The interview is strongest on trade-path risk and the difference between fundamental conviction and realized returns.

Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.

### 029. If premiums rise faster than claims for comparable risks, the loss ratio should improve because it is claims divided by premium.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

Assume matching exposures and periods, positive premium P and claims L. If P grows by p and L by l with p>l, new L/P equals old L/P times (1+l)/(1+p), which is lower. Selection and claim frequency can invalidate the comparable-risk assumption.

## Framework and tools

- Separate company deterioration from profitable trade execution.
- Demand a catalyst rather than shorting solely on valuation.
- Inspect insurance cohorts, state filings and policy exclusions.
- Account for flows and positioning but do not assume they identify every price cause.
- Recognize intellectual attachment to heavily researched shorts.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Short interest and options positioning
- State insurance rate filings and loss ratios
- Enrollment age cohorts
- Store and refrigerator productivity
- Household acquisition cost
- Credit-card panels
- Price/book and price/earnings comparisons
- Policy exclusions and legal filings
- Charts and technical breakouts
